manual.concrete.line2: {0}Concrete is a very hard and resistant composite material. It's cheap to craft and makes for an excellent use for crushed excess {1}slag{2} produced by making steel.
manual.concrete.line3: {0}Concrete can be cut and assembled into various bricks and pillars using the §2Stonecutter§r.{1}
manual.concrete.line4: Concrete bricks have the same blast resistance as concrete, but can be disassembled faster than their solid counterpart, making them a good structural material.
manual.concrete.line5: {0}Concrete can be cut into slabs of varying thickness using a §2Stonecutter§r.{1}
manual.concrete.line6: You can also use that machine to make slabs and stairs of concrete, as well as concrete tiles which are smoother and more polished.
manual.concrete.line7: {0}Lead plating added to concrete, makes it a little more resistant to explosions.{1}
manual.concrete.line8: More importantly however, it prevents etheric energies from penetrating it, blocking any teleporting through it for End-creatures, Ender Pearls and Chorus Fruits.
manual.concrete.line9: {0}Reinforced concrete is made from {1}liquid concrete{2} shaped around bars of §2Netherite§r, making it highly resistant to even powerful explosions like those of a Wither.
manual.concrete.line10: {0}Liquid concrete can be produced in a {1}Mixer{2} by combining half a bucket of Water with §2Gravel§r, §2Clay§r and §2two pieces of Sand§r. When emptied onto the ground it will spread like water, before solidifying after some time.{3}
manual.concrete.line11: Multiple buckets can be used to fill a larger area by placing it at key locations.
manual.concrete.line12: Note that if it spreads too thin, the liquid will dry into slabs instead of full blocks.{0}
manual.concrete.line13: If the concrete dries while a creature is standing in it, they will be trapped and unable to move. You can also fill a {0}Chemical Thrower{1} with liquid concrete in order to create improvised platforms or immobilize enemies.
